from: October book, night 13 (The Trees Clap Their Hands)
p1: Sometimes the Lord’s people did not understand His plans. So the Lord spoke to them through Isaiah.
The Lord said, “My thoughts are not your thoughts.” Look up at the sky. It is so much higher than the ground!
The Lord said His thoughts are higher than ours, just like that. He knows much more than we do. So we can trust Him.
p2: Isaiah said, “You shall go out with joy.” The mountains would sing, and the trees would clap their hands! Trees do not really have hands. Isaiah meant the whole earth would be glad, like leaves rustling in the wind.
You can trust the Lord, even when things feel hard. Tonight, clap your hands softly and say, “I trust You.”
old: Long ago, Heavenly Father's people had to live far away from home in a land called Babylon. They had been there a long, long time, and now it was almost time to go home! Isaiah was Heavenly Father's prophet — that means a man Heavenly Father tells things to, so he can tell the people. Isaiah said, "Look for the Lord while you can find Him. Talk to Him while He is close." Looking for the Lord just means praying to Heavenly Father and following Jesus. Isaiah was talking about Jesus, who was coming to save us all.

Heavenly Father said, "My thoughts are bigger than your thoughts. They are as high as the sky is above the ground." He meant: I can see the whole plan, and you can only see today. The people were worried about the long walk home. Heavenly Father was telling them, you do not have to see it all — you can trust Me.

Then Heavenly Father used a picture everybody there knew. "Rain and snow come down from the sky. They do not go back up empty. They water the ground, the seeds grow, and there is bread to eat." That land was dry and dusty, so rain meant food on the table. Everybody loved rain. That is why Heavenly Father picked rain for His picture.

"My words are like that rain," Heavenly Father said. "They always do the job I send them to do." So when He promised His people would go home happy and safe, the promise was sure. Heavenly Father keeps His word every single time.

Isaiah said the mountains would sing and the trees would clap their hands. Mountains and trees cannot really sing or clap. That was Isaiah's happy way of saying the people were SO glad that even the hills seemed to cheer. Tonight you can be glad too, safe and warm in your bed, because Heavenly Father is near you right now.
